title: Network Redundancy: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: Every car needs a spare tyre. A network needs spares as well. That's called redundancy.

scenes.heading: The spare tyre
scenes.narration: Each layer has its own way of being redundant. Spanning tree stops loops, with a hello of two seconds. Rapid S T P recovers in one to three seconds. H S R P gives hosts a gateway that survives failure. Ether channel bundles links, so one failing doesn't matter.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three traps. It reduces downtime, not removes it. Classic S T P is slow to recover. A single link is a single point of failure.

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.narration: So, to recap. Add a spare at every layer. R S T P is much faster than S T P. Test the backups. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva redundancy lab.
